title_ar: شرح ورقات إمام الحرمين في أصول الفقه الشريط الخامس
title_en: Commentary on the Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn on legal theory — tape five
body_ar:
الآحاد:

والآحاد جمع أحد وهو الواحد ، (والمقصود بالآحاد في اصطلاح الأصوليين) ، و المقصود بخبر الآحاد في اصطلاح الأصوليين ما رواه آحاد من الناس لا يصلون إلى درجة التواتر ، ولهذا عرفه بقوله: والآحاد هو الذي يوجب العمل ولا يوجب العلم ، فقد قسم الخبر إلى قسمين إلى متواتر ، و خبر آحاد ، فالآحاد هنا على حذف مضاف تقديره خبر الآحاد هو الذي يوجب العمل ولا يوجب العلم ، والمقصود هنا بإيجاب العمل أي على فرض صحته ، واقتضائه الوجوب ، فالآحاد ليس بالضرورة صحيحا حتى يوجب العمل ، وقوله ولا يوجب العلم أي ما لم يحتف بالقرائن فقد يحتف خبر الآحاد بالقرائن ، فيقتضي العلم الضروري كذلك كما رواه مالك عن نافع عن ابن عمر ، وما اتفق على إخراجه البخاري ومسلم من أخبار الآحاد ، فقد احتف به من القرائن ما يقتضي الثقة به حتى يكون كالمتواتر ، فيحصل به العلم ، وهذا العلم نظري لا ضروري ...
body_en:
The singly transmitted:

Al-āḥād is the plural of aḥad, which means "one". (And what is meant by al-āḥād in the terminology of the legal theorists) — what is meant by the singly transmitted report in the terminology of the legal theorists is what individuals among the people have narrated who do not reach the degree of mass transmission. It is for this reason that he defined it by his words: "And the singly transmitted is that which necessitates action but does not necessitate knowledge." He divided the report into two divisions: into the mass-transmitted, and the singly transmitted report. So al-āḥād here involves the elision of a governed noun, the implied sense being: the singly transmitted report is that which necessitates action but does not necessitate knowledge. What is meant here by its necessitating action is: on the assumption of its soundness, and of its entailing obligation — for the singly transmitted is not necessarily sound, such that it should necessitate action. And his words "and does not necessitate knowledge" mean: so long as it is not attended by supporting indications. For a singly transmitted report may be attended by indications, and so entail necessary knowledge as well, as with what Malik narrated from Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, and what al-Bukhari and Muslim agreed upon recording among the singly transmitted reports; for there attends it such indications as entail confidence in it, so that it becomes like the mass-transmitted, and knowledge is obtained by it — and this knowledge is theoretical, not necessary ...

flags.arabic: فيقتضي العلم الضروري كذلك ... وهذا العلم نظري لا ضروري
flags.context: the closing two clauses of the published text, which appear to contradict each other
options: translate both as printed and flag the contradiction
read the first occurrence as 'necessitates knowledge' without al-ḍarūrī
read the first occurrence as al-ʿilm al-yaqīnī ('certain knowledge')
flags.note: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IN THE SOURCE, SUBSTANTIVE. The passage first says that a singly transmitted report attended by supporting indications 'entails necessary knowledge' (al-ʿilm al-ḍarūrī), and then concludes that 'this knowledge is theoretical, not necessary' (naẓarī lā ḍarūrī). As printed the two statements cannot both stand. The concluding clause is the settled position of the majority of legal theorists, which suggests the word al-ḍarūrī in the earlier clause is an intrusion by the transcriber. Under the rule against silently repairing the source both have been translated as printed. This must be resolved against the audio before publication, because as it stands the passage attributes a self-contradictory position to the Sheikh on a central question of the discipline.

flags.context: a clause in round brackets, immediately repeated in fuller form outside the brackets
options: preserve the bracketed clause and the repetition, as printed
treat the bracketed clause as an editorial insertion and remove it
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The bracketed clause is a partial duplicate of the sentence that immediately follows it — the signature of a transcription in which a phrase was set down, then restarted and completed. body_ar preserves it and body_en carries it in brackets so the duplication is visible to a reviewer rather than tidied away.

flags.context: the definition of the singly transmitted report that the whole passage turns on
options: necessitates action but does not necessitate knowledge
obliges action but does not yield knowledge
makes action obligatory but does not make knowledge obligatory
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR THE FIVE-RULINGS MAPPING. Yūjib here is the logical 'entails, necessitates', not the legal ruling 'makes obligatory'. Option 2 applies the five-rulings table and produces nonsense, since knowledge is not the sort of thing a report can make obligatory. Option 1 is half right but 'obliges' still leans on the legal sense. The Sheikh himself then uses wujūb in the legal sense two clauses later ('and of its entailing obligation'), so both senses are live within three lines, which is exactly the hazard the style guide's addendum describes for creedal contexts. See the note below.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on al-Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni, a short primer on legal theory. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 649–652 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and tape two does not appear anywhere in the range 601–652.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

IMPORTANT FOR THE FIVE-RULINGS MAPPING. In this material yūjib and wujūb are used in their logical sense, of one thing entailing or necessitating another, and not as the legal ruling 'obligatory'. 'A singly-transmitted report necessitates action but does not necessitate knowledge' is a statement about what follows from the report, not a ruling that acting on it is obligatory. Applying the five-rulings table here would misread the sentence, in the same way that the style guide's addendum warns against applying it to wājib in creedal contexts.

'Necessary' and 'theoretical' render ḍarūrī and naẓarī as kinds of knowledge — the first immediate and compelling, the second arrived at by inference. Note that ḍarūrī here has nothing to do with the glossary's ḍarūrah, 'necessity' as a legal threshold permitting the otherwise forbidden. This is the fourth homonym trap found in this slice, after ʿilal at id 629, muṭlaq at id 636 and adāʾ at id 645.

'What Malik narrated from Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar' is the chain traditionally called the golden chain, cited here as the standing example of a singly transmitted report carrying exceptional confidence. The Sheikh does not name it as such and no name has been supplied.
'Supporting indications' renders qarāʾin, as at id 650.
The record opens with a bare heading and no doxology, so the beginning of the lecture is not published.
